title: C vs Python diverge on unjoined-foreign-DODAG first contact (C rejects, Python adopts)
description: Found by correctness+security codereview of zt3c.7.6 (both passes independently). Pre-existing behavioral divergence, touched by the 02xx test migration but not introduced by it. On identical input (unjoined node dodag_id=X version=5; foreign DIO same instance, dodag_id=Y != X, version=0, rank=256): C lichen_rpl_dodag_process_dio REJECTS the foreign DODAG outright — lichen/subsys/lichen/rpl/dodag.c:410-412 'if (foreign) return 0;' applies regardless of join state, and test test_unjoined_foreign_dodag_rejected (lichen/tests/rpl_dodag/main.c:455) pins rejection — while Python DodagState.process_dio ADOPTS the foreign DODAGID on first contact (self._adopt_version(dio), python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py:423-426; test test_unjoined_foreign_dodag_is_not_version_compared python/tests/rpl/test_dodag.py:431-444 asserts adoption). Compounding: the C comment at dodag.c:400-405 says 'An UNJOINED node may first-join a foreign DODAG' — contradicting the code below it; and the C test header (main.c:12-14) claims parity with python/tests/rpl/test_dodag.py which is false for this case. One side's semantics is wrong per RFC 6550 8.2.1/3.2.3 (a node should be able to join any DODAG it hears; C's init-pinned DODAGID assumes out-of-band provisioning). Needs a spec decision: which behavior is canonical, then fix impl+tests+comment on the other side and restore the documented cross-impl parity. All touched tests currently use 0200:: native addresses consistently on both sides.
